page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 4 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, rank in the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, data compression and decompression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3, show weak to poor performance. However, memory subsystem performance is relatively stronger, with the PassMark memory score reaching the average category, though raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks remain in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g6.xlarge offers a predictable resource profile for entry-level enterprise workloads. Because it lacks local storage and exhibits weak performance in compute-intensive and database operations, it is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, basic web serving, or development environments where high-throughput processing is not a primary requirement.
